sentences.text: Shamosuchus was a crocodylomorph that grew up to four meters long and possessed a rostrum of moderate length.
In the species S. djadochtaensis, the alveolar margin at the premaxilla-maxilla articulation is continuous and lacks a notch for the opposing mandibular tooth.
Its eyes and nostrils were not positioned above the skull, requiring it to lift its entire head out of the water to breathe.
Its cranial morphology suggests Shamosuchus was not an ambush predator but likely fed on aquatic invertebrates.
The genus Shamosuchus was named by Charles C. Mook in 1924.
Shamosuchus lived in the Djadochta Formation of Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous, roughly 75 to 71 million years ago.
It inhabited the Gobi Desert of Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 85 to 66 million years ago.
The time range for Shamosuchus spans from the Cenomanian to the Maastrichtian, between 100.5 and 66 million years ago.
Recent cladistic analysis suggests that the genus Paralligator is distinct from Shamosuchus, despite previous synonymization.
